sub: Paris, thirteen oh three.
It is getting dark, and you are twelve years old.
In front of you is a piece of silk with
gold thread in it, half finished.
On the table there is a candle.
You are not allowed to light it.
That is not your master being cheap.
It is the law.
This year the embroiderers of Paris wrote it into their
rules: no work by candlelight.
Here is the reason they give.
Work done by candlelight comes out worse than work done
by day.
A candle is yellow, and it moves.
A crooked stitch can look straight.
So when the light goes,
the needle goes down.
In June, that is a long day.
In December, it is a short one.
You will do this for eight years.
That is what an ordinary life is.
Not small.
Just made, very carefully, in daylight.
